::: {.why}
Purging removes training observations whose labels overlap the test period; embargoing removes ones that follow it. Both are needed, they solve different problems, and conflating them is the standard mistake.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement purged and embargoed cross-validation and state which leakage each part prevents.
- Justify the embargo length from a measured property of your data rather than from a convention.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement `PurgedKFold` in qlib/ml/cv.py, compatible with the scikit-learn splitter interface so it drops into any search: purge training observations whose label windows overlap the test window, then embargo a fixed number of observations after the test window. Test it by rerunning yesterday's pure-noise experiment and confirming the cross-validated R-squared returns to zero.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Set the embargo from the data: measure the autocorrelation of your labels and of your features, and choose the embargo as the lag at which both have decayed. Report the number and the measurement behind it. An embargo picked by convention is a parameter you cannot defend in an interview.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/ml/cv.py provides a purged and embargoed splitter with the scikit-learn interface, so every model search in the phase uses it by default and the noise experiment from day 205 is a standing test that it works.
:::
